## Set Up

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

## Load packages

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(sampling)

# if either package is not installed, it can be done by
# install.packages('sampling')
# install.packages('ggplot2')
```

## Draw a SRS

This is just one way to accomplish drawing a SRS.

```{r}
# draw a simple random sample (without replacement) of size 20 
# from a population of size 500

sample(1:500, size=20, replace=FALSE)
```

## Example: Swiss Municipalities

This population provides information about the Swiss municipalities in 2003. It is a data frame with 2896 observations on 22 variables, including things like area under cultivation, area with buildings, number of households, etc.

```{r}
?swissmunicipalities				# info about data

data(swissmunicipalities)			# load data
```

#### 1. Consider the area under cultivation for each municipality.

```{r}
# area under cultivation
areacult <- swissmunicipalities$Surfacescult	

# print the first 200
areacult[1:200]
```

#### 2. Draw a SRS of size 100

```{r}
n <- 100
N <- length(areacult)

# this will return the indices of the samples observations
samp <- sample(1:N, size=n, replace=FALSE)

# print the names of the first 40 sampled municipalities
names <- swissmunicipalities$Nom
names[samp[1:40]]
```

#### 3. Draw a SRS of size 100

```{r}
# print the areas under cultivation for the sampled municipalities
areacult[samp]
```

#### 4. Estimate the population total using our sample

```{r}
t.hat1 <- N * mean(areacult[samp])
t.hat1

# calculate the actual population total
t <- sum(areacult)
t
```

#### 5. Let's draw 10 more samples

```{r fig.height=4, fig.width=5, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, out.width='400px', dpi=300, fig.align="center"}
t.hat <- rep(0, 10)
for (i in 1:10) {
	samp.new <- sample(1:N, size=n, replace=FALSE)
	t.hat[i] <- N * mean(areacult[samp.new])
}

ggplot(data.frame(t.hat), aes(x=t.hat)) + 
  geom_histogram() + theme_bw() + 
  geom_vline(xintercept=t, col="red")
```

#### 6. Let's draw many MANY more samples

```{r fig.height=4, fig.width=5, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, out.width='400px', dpi=300, fig.align="center"}
t.hat <- rep(0, 100000)
for (i in 1:100000) {
	samp.new <- sample(1:N, size=n, replace=FALSE)
	t.hat[i] <- N * mean(areacult[samp.new])
}

ggplot(data.frame(t.hat), aes(x=t.hat)) + 
  geom_histogram() + theme_bw() +
  geom_vline(xintercept=t, col="red")
```
